about: The camera page's signed release list: docs/API.md (The camera page), docs/WEB-CAMERA.md § 2. A temporary camera's code is a page, served by a host of its own. Before a viewer shows any code for one, and again before it gives one more time, it fetches the release document from under the page's address, checks it as below, then fetches the page's address and every listed file and checks each against the list. Anything that fails, and it shows no code.

The document is JSON: {"v": 1, "list": "<the list, as text>", "signatures": [{"key": "<a release key, X9.63 uncompressed, base64url>", "sig": "<base64url of r || s, 64 bytes>"}]}. A signature is ECDSA over P-256 with SHA-256 over the UTF-8 of "petcam.release.v1|" followed by the list's text exactly as it came. A release is signed if one of the first eight signatures is by a key the build carries (matched by its bytes, checked with the build's own copy) and holds. Nothing of the list is read before that.

The list is JSON too: {"v": 1, "page": "<the page's address>", "release": <1 … 2^31 − 1>, "entry": "<the file the page's address serves>", "files": [{"path": "<under the page's address>", "sha256": "<lowercase hex>", "bytes": <length>}]}. A path is file names of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - joined by "/", none of them "." or "..", 128 characters at most; a list has 1 to 64 files of at most 8 MB each, none named twice, its entry among them.

`expect` is "takes", or why not: "not_signed" (no signature by a key this build carries holds), "not_a_release" (the document or its list isn't one), "another_page" (signed for another address than the build's), "too_old" (below the oldest release the build takes), "older_than_seen" (below the newest this device has taken); and for what the host serves, "served", "file_missing" or "file_changed". A document that isn't one is turned away first; then the signature; then the list's own shape, its page, the build's oldest and the newest seen, in that order. The first that fails decides.

The signature is P-256 because that is the one curve a Mac's keychain and its Secure Enclave hold as a key that signs without giving up its bytes, and CryptoKit, Java, Android and Web Crypto all check it with nothing added; r || s because it has one form and one length where DER has several. The real key is made on one Mac and is in no file. The keys here were made up for this file: they sign nothing real.
Bytes are base64url without padding unless a field says hex (a list's `sha256` is lowercase hex, as shasum prints it); strings are UTF-8; "|" joins the parts of a message, with nothing around it.

Made by server/scripts/vectors.mjs from fixed keys that were made up for these files; nothing here was ever a real home's. No vector is ever removed: a format the apps stop opening stays, as one that must fail. The page's address here, https://camera.example/petcam/, is no real host's. Read by SharedTests/PageReleaseVectorTests.swift, server/test/vectors.test.ts and android/core's PageReleaseVectorTest.kt.

keys.how: P-256 signing keys, each 32 bytes of one value: test keys. `build` in each case names the ones it carries.

spare.what: a second key a build may carry too

release.how: Release 3 as it would be published: its files, the list made from them, and the document that carries the list and its signature. `signed` is exactly what the signature is over.

how: Before it fetches anything, a viewer asks where the page's name points. It looks up the name and the host the name must point at (GitHub's own name for the organization's pages, which the name is a CNAME to) together, through the device's own resolver, asking for every address of both. Every address the name has must be one of the host's: `points_at_its_host`. One that isn't: `name_elsewhere`. No address for either: `name_unresolved`. Refused either way, no code shows and nothing is fetched.

Addresses are compared as bytes, 4 for IPv4 and 16 for IPv6, with an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address taken as its IPv4. `addresses` gives the bytes of every address written here, in hex. The two answers are compared with each other and never with addresses a build carries: a host's addresses change, and a resolver on an IPv6-only network writes them its own way.

What it buys: pointing the name elsewhere for everyone starts no camera anywhere, since no viewer shows a code. It doesn't see a name answered one way for a camera's network and another for its viewer's (docs/SECURITY.md, Limits).
The names here are stand-ins, and the addresses are from the ranges kept for documentation.

serving.how: Release 3, taken, against what the host serves: `served.address` is what the page's address itself answered with, and `served.files` what each path under it did (null or absent: nothing). The address has to serve the entry file, and each listed path its file, each the length and the SHA-256 the list gives.

cases.why: the page's address serves the entry file, and every listed path its file

cases.name: another_page_at_the_address

ecdsa.how: The signature itself, checked alone: ECDSA over P-256 with SHA-256 over the UTF-8 of `message`, `signature` being r || s. The first two are RFC 6979's own (A.2.5), which this script's signer reproduces.

cases.why: RFC 6979, A.2.5: P-256 with SHA-256, "sample". Its s is the larger of the two that verify: a signature isn't held to the smaller
